notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from five pages. Cliopatria has no Shanxi row, so this dossier draws Shanxi province as a state for 38 years; the ROC row (ea-08-c) draws it as part of China, and its dossier carries vassal events for the Guangxi clique, Guominjun and Fengtian clique only (Yan Xishan is not listed there). Not settled: (1) the Shanxi clique page's infobox 'Active: 1911-1937' against 'Disbanded: 1949': this dossier lasts to 1949; (2) the 1928 gains: the page's 'all the way to the sea at Hebei and Shandong' has no date and the Northern Expedition page does not credit Yan's troops, so the event is at confidence 2 on the strength of the page's own sentence; Shandong is left out; (3) what Yan held between the Northeast Army's entry in September 1930 and 1937 (his return to power is not on the pages; the shape is plain Shanxi); (4) the recovery of the occupied land in 1945 (confidence 1); (5) the month of the 1949 fall (Taiyuan's fall is not dated on the pages); (6) Suiyuan, Chahar and Rehe, which the Kuomintang may have allowed Yan to hold in 1928-1930, are not on the pages. The ruler strip is one name; it is documented only by the two Yan pages. A gap-filler should open 'Taiyuan campaign (1949)' and 'Yan Xishan' sections on 1930-1931. Gazetteer: all names resolved.

[ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, after the adversarial review (verdict fail)] (1) Vassal events added from the vassal's side: kuomintang 1928-6 to 1929-12 and republic-of-china 1930 to 1930-5 (mirrors kuomintang /ledger/21 and /27, republic-of-china /ledger/29 and /35). (2) Hebei and Tianjin: the 1930-9 loss is widened to Hebei, Beijing and Tianjin (the whole of the 1928 gain) on the Zhang Xueliang page; the Fengtian side is widened to match. (3) The 1937 loss and the 1945 gain are retyped occupation_start/occupation_end with counterpart empire-of-japan, as the Japan dossier types them; the end is dated 30 August 1945 from the Yan Xishan page (Japan's mirror says September). (4) Capital strips split: Taiyuan 1911-1937, an unnamed south-west base 1938-1944 (a coordinate at the centre of the ring, not a place: neither Yan page names the town), Taiyuan 1945-1949. (5) The Taiyuan campaign page, opened for the thin item, shows the shape was not 'all Shanxi' in 1948-1949: a new keyframe 1948-1949 is two circles (Taiyuan, Datong) and a 1948 loss to communist-party-of-china at confidence 1 (the page does not date the Central Shanxi campaign); the dissolve is now 24 April 1949 (month and land from the page; the first notes said the month was unknown). (6) Not settled: the date and extent of the 1928 Hebei gain; the Yan Xishan page (opened) says only that Chiang let Yan 'expand his influence into Hebei' without a date, does not mention the Northern Expedition, Beijing or Tianjin, and does not mention Yan's exile or his return in 1931-1932; the gain stays at confidence 2 and the 1931-1937 shape stays plain Shanxi. Gazetteer name still needed: none new.
